title: Pseudophakic Bullous Keratopathy (PBK) & Post-Phaco Corneal Edema
summary: Post-phacoemulsification corneal edema is a clinical challenge involving corneal decompensation due to endothelial cell loss. Mastery of this condition is essential for recognizing the transition from transient postoperative edema to permanent bullous keratopathy.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Corneal edema post-phacoemulsification results from acute endothelial decompensation. The corneal endothelium (average density 2000–3000 cells/mm²) possesses limited regenerative capacity. Mechanical trauma (phaco-burn), chemical toxicity (inadequate irrigation fluid, preservatives like benzalkonium chloride), or preexisting endothelial dystrophy (Fuchs') causes sodium-potassium pump failure, leading to stromal hydropic swelling and potential epithelial bullae formation.

sections.title: Clinical Features
content: Decreased vision (especially upon awakening)
Foreign body sensation or pain (if bullae rupture)
Striae in Descemet's membrane
Stromal haze (ground glass appearance)
Epithelial microcysts and macrobullae
Peripheral anterior synechiae (advanced cases)

sections.title: Red Flag Symptoms
content: Infection/Endophthalmitis (pain, hypopyon, vitritis)
Acute IOP spike > 40 mmHg causing epithelial edema
Wound dehiscence/Seidel-positive leaking wound
Choroidal detachment/hemorrhage
Unexplained persistent pain requiring topical NSAIDs or hypertonics

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Sequence
content: Step 1: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy (Assess stromal thickness and bullae).
Step 2: Pachymetry (Baseline central corneal thickness: >650μm indicates significant edema).
Step 3: Specular Microscopy (Quantify endothelial cell density and hexagonality).
Step 4: Intraocular Pressure Measurement (Rule out ocular hypertension).
Step 5: Gonioscopy (Check for synechiae or retained nuclear fragments).

rows: Presence of hypopyon and severe vitritis
High IOP, closed angle, narrow chamber

content.explanation: Assessment: Anatomy (Check angle/IOL), Bullae (check extent), Cell count (Specular), Density (Pachymetry), Edema (Epithelial vs Stromal)

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: If edema is present on POD 1, check the IOP first.
Hypertonic saline (5%) is most effective for epithelial bullae.
A quiet, normotensive eye with edema usually requires wait-and-see for 3-6 months.
Endothelial cell loss is usually 10-25% in uncomplicated cases.
DMEK is the current gold standard for endothelial keratoplasty.
